Letter dated May 3, 1972, to the State Clearinghouse from Director,
Sanitary Engineering Division, North Carolina State Board of Health.
Comment: The North Carolina State Board of Health is concerned that protection and development of habitat for endangered species will encourage vectors of human disease. In the statement prepared by the Director of Sanitary Engineering Division of the Board, a number of qualifying clauses are proposed for inclusion in the EIS. These clauses would require that land acquired for endangered species habitat not be allowed to produce such vectors; that land alterations existing on such tracts at the time of acquisition or vector control (presumably drainage ditches) must be maintained and; that if conditions favoring vectors develop on such lands, alleviation of these conditions shall be permitted.
Response: Flat acceptance of such conditions could render some habitats sterile as far as production of the desired endangered species is concerned. If habitat for that endangered species is at a premium, strict qualifications for vector control could greatly inhibit or even destroy any restoration of the species. Such rigid qualifications are not required to protect humans from disease. Each case must be treated individually depending upon: (1) the endangered species involved, its status and distribution; (2) the human disease involved and its prevalence; (3) the vector involved and its relationship to the endangered species and the disease; (4) the remoteness of the site to human habitation and the surrounding density of human habitation; (5) the compatibility of vector control to the welfare of the endangered species; and (6) consideration of alternative methods of vector control.
